steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Process 1 cup flour, butter, and 1/4 cup confectioners' sugar in a food processor for 10 seconds, or blend with a pastry blender until a dough forms. Pat dough evenly into a 9-inch round pie plate.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden, 12 to 15 minutes.
While crust bakes, combine eggs, white sugar, lemon juice, lemon zest, and 3 tablespoons flour; mix until smooth. Pour egg mixture over hot crust.
Bake in the preheated oven until firm, 15 to 20 minutes more. Let cool completely in pie dish, about 1 to 2 hours. Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons confectioners' sugar and cut into 12 triangles.

raw_recipe.headline: Tart Lemon Triangles
raw_recipe.description: These tart lemon "pies" are basically triangle-shaped lemon bars with a shortbread crust, both lemon juice and zest, and baked in a pie plate.

video.description: Watch how to make Melissa's recipe for Tart Lemon Triangles. The base is a quick pie crust that's filled with a delicious lemon custard. Just bake it and let it cool completely. Then cut this tart into triangles and dust with powdered sugar for the perfect finish.
video.name: Tart Lemon Triangles

review.reviewBody: I like to have something lemon for dessert on Easter, and since I don't do meringue well I decided to try this in place of lemon meringue pie. I expected something more like a pie, which this is not. However, my review is based on the actual product, not my expectations. I thought the taste of the lemon was excellent--nice and tart. Unlike some other reviewers, I didn't find the crust to be crumbly. I think the secret is cutting the butter in well and pressing the crumbs down firmly to form the crust. I thought the crust was a little too sweet. Personally, I don't think the lemon layer is thick enough in relation to the crust, and if I made this again I might double the filling amount.

Very good. It was easy and it makes for a nicer presentation than lemon bars. I did use a bit more zest, but followed the rest exactly. The crust to filling ratio was correct for my 1 0" tart pan. I will go a bit more up the sides next time. I made the filling in the food processor so it was super easy to clean-up. 15 min for the crust and 20 for filling was perfect in my oven.

These were great! I made as directed, except for using 1/2 cup butter (since other reviewers mentioned the crust was a bit crumbly), and a bit extra lemon juice (I used juice and zest from 3 lemons since others noted they liked them more sour.) Oh, and I also added a pinch of salt to the crust and the filling. I used a pastry blender for the crust, just like making a pie crust, which I would recommend. It's easy and less messy than using a food processor since you can just toss it in the dishwasher. I cooked them a little bit longer, just until the filling was set. They were absolutely delicious. UPDATE: Still one of my favorite recipes, and I tried replacing half of the sugar (powdered and granulated) with granulated Splenda. I'm here to report that it was fantastic. I can't even taste the difference. I didn't replace it all w/Spenda because I wasn't sure if the original sugar was needed for browning or texture. I'll make them this way from now on. Less sugar, less guilt!

I followed the recipe with 1 small exception of using a full stick of softened butter 1/2 cup (vs 3/8 cup per recipe). I am glad I used more butter for the crust, because it still seemed quite dry when pressing it down. This is an easy recipe, the hardest part is trying to evenly spread the crust on the bottom and sides of the pie plate. 15 mins bake time for crust and 22 mins bake time for filling was perfect. I got rave reviews from my family on this, and I will definitely be adding to my favorite deserts folder! The crust is sooo good, it's got just the right amount of lemon flavor, and totally satisfied my lemon craving. YUMMM!

This cookie is practically perfect! Bake til lightly browned for tender and chewy, or add a couple of minutes for a crunchier milk-dipper. Either way, they're really great. Boost the health factor by subbing 1 1/2 c whole wheat pastry flour and 1/2 c unbleached flour, evaporated cane sugar, unsalted butter plus 1/3 t sea salt, and agave nectar for the corn syrup. If you stir the dry ingredients into the wet just until you don't see any more powder - no longer, and refrigerate the dough for an hour, you won't be disappointed with tough cookies. :)

These were pretty good. I used Meyer Lemon zest and juice, decreased the sugar by 2 Tbs, added an extra tsp of zest and 1/2 tsp of vanilla extract. After cooling I topped the filling with freshly beaten stabilized whipped cream with 1 tsp of Meyer Lemon zest and 2 Tbs of powdered sugar added then chilled it in the fridge before cutting. A 9" pie plate makes 6 not 12 servings.

I have to say that this is the first recipe that I made on All Recipes that I didn't love. I made the recipe as written, except doubled the filling as recommended by a number of reviewers. The main thing that I didn't like about it was that it was just TOO SWEET. For me, the sweetness just overpowered any tart flavor that you would get from the lemon. I may try this again with less sugar, but I'm not sure. There are just too many other recipes that I want to try! Doubling the filling was a good idea in my opinion. However, my 12 year old son who NEVER comments on food said "it's pretty good, but it seems like there is too much filling and not enough crust" so go figure! 

2nd time around -- decided to try it again with less sugar - I used 1.5 cups total and cooked for 40 minutes (doubled filling again) and put into a pre-made graham cracker crust.

I made it this with raw sugar, GF all purpose flour and no zest because that’s what I had. I made it in the food processor and let it whirl for over a minute thinking it would break up and dissolve the raw sugar. It created a foamy top that baked into a delicate crunchy topping! I think it could have used more lemon but maybe if I had had some zest the flavor would have been stronger. Nevertheless it was verrrry tasty! The crust was just right, not tough nor too fragile. I pressed it down firmly only to the first edge of the rim. When I poured in the custard, it came to within less than half an inch of the edge. I could see where if you made the crust to the top rim you could easily double the filling and it may be even more tasty because of the different ratio of filling to crust.

The recipe was good, but I did change a few things. I added also half squeeze lemon to the filing. And the crust I use 1/4 cup of shortening and half stick of butter, 1/4 teaspoon of salt, then I stired in cold water slowly till it got to the mosit I like. Chilled it for 30 minutes. It work well with the tart.
I added 2tspns more butter than the recipe called in the crust because it seemed too dry. I also reduced the sugar to 3/4 cups. Tasted perfect!!!!

Made a few changes to the filling: used 1/2 cup of lemon juice, reduced sugar to 3/4 cup to cut down the sweetness and increased flour to 1/4 cup. Tastes so good with a nice balance of sweet and tangy. This is definitely going into my recipe box. Thank you

I do NOT like the burnt crust Wish I would have sprayed the pie plate first as it stuck around the edges. I added a couple of heaping tablespoons of lemon curd I happened to have. the filling took more like 50 minutes to bake I had to put aluminum foil around the edges. People really seemed to like it. I did dust with powered sugar and a couple of raspberries on top. I’ll look for another lemon tart recipe
I’ve tried multiple recipes for lemon bars and never found one that worked well. This is the best! It was easy and absolutely delicious! I’ve found my favorite.

When I make a lemon dessert, I really want strong lemon flavor. As usual, I cut the sugar somewhat in the filling (just trying to cut back some) and it was still sweet enough. I added extra lemon zest and a touch of lemon extract to up the punch, and it worked well. The only problem here is the amount of butter in the crust. It was very, very sand-like before I added another 1-2 tablespoons full to the mix.
This was so so amazing. I preferred it with almond flour mixed into the reg flour. Great flavor
Very yummy! Cooked it for exactly 20 minutes and it turned out perfect.
Easy and tasty
We loved it! Fast, easy, and delicious.

Great recipe and even better the next day. I love lemon so next time I may add a bit more juice but I found the crust to be delicious and the filling satisfying. If anyone is having trouble getting the filling to come together I recommend using an electric mixer to smooth it out. Enjoy!

Filling was way too sweet for me and I didn't add the powdered sugar dusting. I used about 1/2 c lemon juice, but it just tasted sugary, then eggy. The crust seems dry when you make it, but it works out and tastes good. Maybe add a dash of salt to the crust to cut the sweetness of the filling? Was not lemony enough. Was easy, but won't make again.
